newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BCE to trade Czech crown futures May 22.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BCE to trade Czech crown futures May 22.

text.p: The Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) will start trading Czech crown futures on Thursday, BCE officials said on Wednesday.

"This will be a pioneering move in the region and we will have to establish close links between Hungarian and Czech banks," Szergej Keresztesi, President of the BCE Council, told a news conference following the BCE's general meeting.
Referring to recent turmoil around the Czech crown, he added that although the date of the crown listing was an earlier decision, it turned out to be well-timed.
Short-selling pushed the Czech crown to record lows last week, prompting the Czech central bank to intervene.
The BCE has financial, grain and livestock sections, of which the financial section is by far the largest in turnover.
Keresztesi said that in 1996, the BCE jumped to 22nd place in volume terms among the world's futures exchanges from 36th in 1995.

In 1996 the financial section, which trades futures for seven foreign currencies, one- and three-month BUBOR (Budapest Inter-bank Offered Rate) and 90-day interest rates, had a turnover of 855 billion forints, the grains section 62 billion forints and the livestock section 0.6 billion forints.
Keresztesi said that the BCE, the largest commodities exchange in the region, will probably continue the exponential growth it has seen since being established in 1989.
In the first four months of 1997, the BCE's turnover was 353 billion forints, 41 percent above the same period of 1996.
Keresztesi said the BCE was considering gold trading as well and further details might be announced in September.
He also said the BCE and the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) were considering the possibility of a merger and have set up several committees to deal with the issue.
BCE executive director Andrea Varga said an electronic trading system, shortly to be commissioned by the BCE, will be compatible with the BSE.
"Technical experts said that connecting the two systems would cause no problem," she said.
Last year, the futures section of the BSE had a turnover of 190.92 billion forints, while BSE spot turnover was 1,145.444 billion forints.
